description: Width tiers for Languages — Background Language Learner Entry Pathway, Years 9–10
subject: Languages — Background Language Learner Entry

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest honest floor for the descriptor's command term at Y9-10 entry level. For communicating descriptors: the minimum task contexts and interaction types in which the capability is demonstrated. For understanding descriptors: the minimum range of language features or cultural phenomena engaged with analytically.
width_notes.typical_width: The full descriptor scope from ACARA elaborations — what a well-taught Y9-10 background entry class would have engaged with.
width_notes.wider: Enrichment directions adding new task contexts (communicating/creating) or phenomena (understanding). At Y9-10 entry, real community leadership, cross-cultural analysis, and advanced literary engagement are primary width directions.
width_notes.elaborations: ACARA elaborations for the Chinese Background and First Language Learner Entry pathway (Y9-10) used as source data.

AC9LCH10EC01.minimum_width: Participate in a structured debate or discussion using at least two debate strategies and sustaining a reasoned position for at least four turns; participate in at least one spontaneous role-play without a pre-prepared script for at least four turns; produce at least one formal response using appropriate register throughout.
AC9LCH10EC01.typical_width: Apply debate strategies and present balanced arguments; acknowledge and contradict others' views with evidence; share opinions on school and community topics; engage with educational social media; participate in spontaneous hypothetical role-plays; express apology, appreciation and gratitude across contexts; respond formally to correspondence and professional contexts.
wider: Lead a structured debate — facilitating argument, managing challenge, and bringing the discussion to a substantiated conclusion in target language
Compare formal communication conventions in the target language with Australian English professional contexts — identify differences in register markers, structural conventions and sign-off formulas
Participate in a series of progressively more unfamiliar hypothetical scenarios — identify which language resources transferred and which required improvisation
elaborations: applying strategies to sustain face-to-face and secure online conversations
applying effective strategies in a debate, summarising key information and presenting a balanced and reasoned argument
sharing opinions and responding to a range of school-related topics linking ideas to support a view
acknowledging strengths in others' ideas and providing evidence to contradict the ideas
engaging with educational social media to document own experiences and achievements
expressing apology, appreciation or gratitude in diverse ways and comparing practices across contexts
interacting in spontaneous, hypothetical role-plays relating to a range of contexts
responding to a range of texts such as personal letters, emails or job advertisements

AC9LCH10EC02.minimum_width: Contribute to a group discussion using at least two facilitation strategies; contribute at least one substantive entry to a collaborative digital platform and provide justified feedback; contribute to organising a community cultural experience with at least three planning decisions in target language.
AC9LCH10EC02.typical_width: Plan and facilitate live or online events; collaborate to reach agreement by equally contributing ideas; produce bilingual versions of community initiatives; participate in virtual exchanges; negotiate possible sister school connections; contribute to group discussions on social issues with balanced views and evidence; collaboratively write reports and articles.
wider: Lead the organisation of a community cultural event with real community participants — coordinate all planning, promotion, execution and evaluation using target language
Negotiate with a potential sister school or community partner — present a justified recommendation for a specific connection and respond to questions
Research and compare how social issues are discussed and reported in target language media versus Australian English media — identify differences in framing, evidence and perspective
elaborations: planning and facilitating live or secure online events and persuading others to get involved
collaborating to create displays, presentations or performances to showcase learning
using secure online collaborative tools to produce bilingual versions of community initiatives
participating in virtual scenarios related to travelling to target language regions
collaborating to reach agreement by equally contributing ideas for a student-led activity
negotiating possible sister schools and comparing aspects of schools in target language regions
contributing to discussions about social issues to create a group presentation with balanced views
collaboratively writing reports or articles on topics such as the pros and cons of part-time work

AC9LCH10EC03.minimum_width: Evaluate at least two target language texts using explicit credibility criteria and cite at least one source appropriately; participate in at least one structured public speaking or debating task using at least two formal oral strategies.
AC9LCH10EC03.typical_width: Evaluate key messages in contemporary target language media; analyse how rhetorical questions, irony and sarcasm convey meaning; apply understanding of formal text types; evaluate print and digital sources for reliability; use public speaking and debating strategies; role-play scenes demonstrating cultural knowledge; respond to literary texts with analytical and personal depth.
wider: Produce an extended analytical response to a contemporary issue — drawing on multiple sources, applying formal conventions, and evaluating from multiple perspectives
Listen to or read a First Nations Australian author's story in English and present or write a reflective personal response in target language
Prepare and deliver a formal speech or debate contribution on a significant issue — evaluate own performance against identified criteria and revise for a second delivery
elaborations: evaluating key messages in contemporary texts such as magazines, newspapers, websites or podcasts
listening to or reading texts and analysing how language conveys meaning such as rhetorical questions and sarcasm
applying understanding of formal text types to create own response to contemporary issues
listening to or reading a First Nations Australian author's story and presenting a reflective personal response in Chinese
accessing a range of digital and other texts to collate and present information about current affairs
analysing and evaluating information from a range of sources including statistical data
evaluating print or digital resources for reliability and referencing appropriately
exploring how forms of entertainment express or reflect contemporary issues
creating a simplified or more detailed script in response to a film or story

AC9LCH10EC04.minimum_width: Compare at least two translations of the same expression or text and evaluate the difference; interpret at least one exchange in a context requiring cross-cultural knowledge; produce a translation of at least eight sentences or a multimodal bilingual resource with accurate meaning transfer.
AC9LCH10EC04.typical_width: Compare and discuss target language translations of English words and expressions; interpret for events requiring cross-cultural knowledge; compare idioms and colloquialisms across languages; compare bilingual editions of texts; interpret meaning in bilingual contexts; experiment with extended text translation; apply translation strategies in diverse contexts.
wider: Compare own real-world interpreting experience from home and community with structured approaches — identify what is already intuitive and what requires explicit development
Produce a fully subtitled bilingual video — evaluate accuracy and cultural appropriateness with a target audience member and revise accordingly
Research the translation history of a specific culture-specific term — document different translation approaches across contexts and evaluate which works best for which audience
elaborations: comparing and discussing various target language translations of English words, phrases and expressions
identifying words used with specific cultural assumptions such as gender, significance and formality
considering ways to translate culture-specific terms into English
interpreting for target language and English speakers for events requiring cross-cultural knowledge
comparing idioms and colloquialisms across languages and identifying challenges in mediating embedded cultural values
comparing bilingual editions of stories or poems and discussing how authors maintain stylistic devices
interpreting meaning in bilingual contexts and identifying potential issues in mediation
experimenting with translations of extended texts using dictionaries and translation tools
applying translation strategies in target language and English

AC9LCH10EC05.minimum_width: Produce an evaluative or persuasive text with a clear position supported by at least two pieces of evidence; create a procedural text and a community-facing informative text applying correct conventions for each; create a literary or formal text applying at least two conventions from a specific style.
AC9LCH10EC05.typical_width: Create presentations on contemporary issues; produce multimodal presentations using data and statistics; compose texts for events with specific purposes and audiences; create procedural texts; write narratives and biographies applying literary language; create scripts for short plays or video clips; create cultural exhibitions; experiment with formal and subjective language.
wider: Reflect on the protocols required to authentically co-create an Acknowledgement of Country/Place with a First Nations Australian and present it in the target language
Create a multimodal community text for a real external audience — evaluate its effectiveness with stakeholders and revise
Create a text that deliberately applies the conventions of a specific target language literary genre — annotate the stylistic choices and explain the cultural knowledge required
elaborations: creating a presentation on an issue comparing different opinions
producing multimodal presentations using tables, maps, charts or graphs
composing texts for events with specific purposes and audiences
reflecting on the protocols required to authentically co-create an Acknowledgement of Country/Place with a First Nations Australian
writing a narrative account of a character from a book or film
writing a biography of a significant person applying terms from traditional literature
creating a target language voice-over for a scene or collaborating on a drama
composing a script for a short play or video clip
composing and presenting a cultural exhibition for members of the local target language community
experimenting with ways of expressing ideas in formal contexts

AC9LCH10EU01.minimum_width: Demonstrate comprehension of spoken target language from at least two unfamiliar voices or speeds; produce a performance demonstrating deliberate use of at least two prosodic features; deliver a formal speech of at least two minutes with appropriate intonation and stress.
AC9LCH10EU01.typical_width: Listen to interactions between unfamiliar voices at different speeds; discriminate between unfamiliar homophones; identify regional pronunciation variation; experiment with rhythm, pace, tone and stress; take on performance roles; present formal arguments using emphasis and persuasion; read aloud poems in different ways; use digital tools for pronunciation support.
wider: Create an original performance text — rap, spoken word, or monologue — demonstrating deliberate prosodic design choices with annotation explaining each
Compare the prosodic techniques used in target language and English performance genres — identify what is shared and what is culturally specific
Research a specific regional variety of the target language — describe its phonological features and explain comprehension strategies most useful for that variety
elaborations: listening to interactions between unfamiliar voices at different speeds to develop auditory and comprehension skills
discriminating between unfamiliar homophones and enhancing fluency through rap songs or stand-up comedy
identifying regional variation in pronunciation across different target language environments
experimenting with rhythm, pace, tone and stress and developing strategies to enhance communication
using dictionaries or digital tools to help with learning characters and pronunciation
presenting an argument in a debate using emphasis and persuasion with focus on fluency and audience
reading aloud a poem in different ways using intonation to convey happiness, sarcasm or jealousy

AC9LCH10EU02.minimum_width: Predict the meaning of at least three unfamiliar characters using component analysis; compare at least two simplified/traditional form pairs; produce a text demonstrating at least three complex grammatical features correctly including at least one literary or formal register feature.
AC9LCH10EU02.typical_width: Analyse sequences of unfamiliar characters to predict meanings; compare and contrast simplified and traditional character forms; apply word formation understanding in comparing translations; discriminate correct forms and sounds of polysemous characters; explain how morphology conveys subtle meanings; apply advanced punctuation; use literary language; apply tense knowledge across text types.
wider: Investigate a productive morpheme — identify all words it appears in, document the semantic pattern, and explain how morphology conveys subtle and precise meanings
Produce a text that deliberately uses a specific literary grammatical feature for effect — explain the choice and compare with an alternative approach
Analyse own extended writing for grammatical accuracy and register appropriateness — identify patterns and develop a targeted improvement plan
elaborations: analysing sequences of unfamiliar characters to determine features of form and function and predict meanings
comparing and contrasting characters in simplified and traditional forms
analysing and comparing unfamiliar characters in print media and online texts
applying understanding of word formation when comparing translations
discriminating correct forms and sounds of characters with multiple readings
inferring the meaning of unfamiliar words containing a familiar morpheme
explaining how morphology works to convey subtle and precise meanings
inferring meaning of terminology based on character analysis
applying punctuation conventions in writing and reading aloud
using language features to extend and elaborate a point of view
exploring functions of key grammatical forms in different contexts
exploring examples of literary language and how grammatical features differ from everyday speech
experimenting with abstract nouns to create procedural or creative texts

AC9LCH10EU03.minimum_width: Use metalanguage to analyse at least three linguistic features in a target language text; compare content organisation in at least two text types and identify at least two differences from English conventions; identify at least two stylistic devices in a literary text and explain their function.
AC9LCH10EU03.typical_width: Use metalanguage to identify grammatical differences across languages; analyse sequence of content in different text types; explain use of data and evidence in texts; compare how essays are structured across target language and English; analyse language in emails and news articles; explore literary language and how it differs from everyday text; analyse magazine and online text layout.
wider: Compare essay organisation conventions in the target language with English — explain the cultural logic behind the structural differences and apply target language conventions in an original piece
Produce a full stylistic analysis of a target language literary text — annotating every device and evaluating the text's cultural and literary significance
Research a specific literary form unique to the target language tradition — describe its conventions, trace historical origins, and explain cultural significance
elaborations: using metalanguage in Chinese or English to identify the grammatical differences between languages
analysing the sequence of content in different text types such as blogs or news articles
explaining the use of data such as census information and surveys to support views
incorporating statistical data, quotations and research-based evidence in own texts
analysing language used in a range of text types comparing emails for different purposes
analysing language and writing techniques used in traditional target language texts
analysing the layout of magazines and online texts to identify how images and words reinforce ideas
identifying linguistic terms and how world events are reported in target language media
comparing literature across languages and recognising different features
exploring examples of literary language and how grammatical features differ from everyday text

AC9LCH10EU04.minimum_width: Evaluate how at least two cultural traditions or globalisation changes have affected communication; identify at least two examples of language used to empower or marginalise; evaluate at least two ways bilingual identity opens opportunities.
AC9LCH10EU04.typical_width: Evaluate differences in perceptions and communication across cultures; explain how cultural traditions affect communication across target language regions; explore modesty, personal space and respect for authority in communication; reflect on how language may empower or marginalise; identify cultural assumptions embedded in language; evaluate how bilingualism expands world views and creates opportunities.
wider: Reflect on and explain the protocols required to authentically co-create an Acknowledgement of Country/Place with a First Nations Australian — discuss how this process connects to the target language community's own language-culture relationships

Conduct a comparative analysis of how group labels or demographic terms are used across target language and English media — identify differences in framing and discuss the cultural values underlying each
Produce a sustained reflective evaluation of own bilingual identity journey — tracing how it has developed and its significance for future study, community connection and professional aspiration
elaborations: evaluating differences in perceptions, understandings and behaviours across cultures
explaining how cultural traditions and beliefs affect communication of speakers from various regions
exploring how concepts such as modesty, personal space and respect influence communication styles
reflecting on and explaining the protocols required to authentically co-create an Acknowledgement of Country/Place
examining how language may be used to empower or marginalise groups in society
accessing a range of sources and identifying content that creates bias or stereotypes
identifying how knowledge of Chinese and English opens up opportunities to expand world views
exploring cultural assumptions in language such as how terms for 'getting married' differ by gender
analysing own language and cultural backgrounds through conversations with relatives
